note: Every top-level integer constant in every backend gate script, with the direction it may move. check:baseline-integrity fails on an unregistered constant (which is what a rename looks like), a stale registration (the other half of a rename), and any move in the unsafe direction. ratchet = may only decrease. floor = may only increase; lowering a floor is how a gate goes blind while printing OK. pinned = may not change without re-registering, used where the safe direction is genuinely not obvious.

MAX_HOPS.reason: New constant, not a rename — registered 2026-09-04 when this gate's reach went from 2 of 336 paginated GETs to the whole corpus. It caps how many times the payload classifier will follow a return expression through a callback wrapper (runInTenantTransaction, cachedVersioned, withTenant and friends) before giving up and reporting `unresolved`. A ratchet because RAISING it is the dangerous direction: a deeper walk resolves more handlers and so makes the gate look better without any code improving, and an unbounded walk would recurse on a cyclic re-export. Lowering it is safe — it only turns resolved handlers back into honestly-unresolved ones.

RESPONSE_SCHEMA_UNCOVERED_CEILING.owner: every module lane that owns a controller; coordinated by the API contract owner (ticket 04)
RESPONSE_SCHEMA_UNCOVERED_CEILING.reason: Operations declaring NO response body schema. Registered 2026-09-03 by v2 ticket 30 at the TRUE measured figure, 3,617 of 3,642 uncovered (25 covered, 0.69%). The gate previously required 100% and reported 3642/3642 (100%) -- because its predicate accepted a bare 2xx response KEY, which NestJS auto-generates with no content for every handler, so the condition was true for every operation the moment the document was generated. Actual coverage of the property it claimed was 1 in 3,642 (0.027%). This is NOT a baseline raised to turn a regression green: it is the first honest measurement of a number that was never measured, and the 100%% requirement was NOT restored only because demanding it would red the pipeline on ~3,617 handlers across every module lane. Lower it as coverage lands; raising it retires the rule by arithmetic. LOWERED 3617 -> 3613 on 2026-09-04 by v2 ticket 04: the ratchet had been BREACHED at 3,621 because six newly added operations carried no response schema, and it was not raised to absorb them -- ten handlers were given a real @ResponseSchema(...) instead (POST/PUT /calendar/events, PATCH/DELETE /calendar/events/{eventId}/occurrences/{occurrenceStart}, and all six /platform/operator-access operations), each compared against the real handler return by ResponseContractInterceptor under NODE_ENV=test. 3,613 was MEASURED by rebuilding the document in memory from the working tree via generateOpenApiJson() and running this gate's own predicate over it (3,651 operations, 38 covered). It is provisional in one respect and the next reader must know it: the COMMITTED openapi.json still predates both those schemas and three routes other lanes added, so it measures 3,621 and this gate stays RED until the single end-of-wave regenerate -- at which point the figure must be RE-MEASURED and lowered again if it lands below 3,613, never raised if it lands above. CLOSED 2026-09-07: LOWERED 3611 -> 0. Every one of the 3,666 operations now declares a response body schema, measured by regenerating openapi.json from the working tree and running this gate over it. Two mechanisms were added to make the count honest rather than merely large: @NoContentResponse() stamps a 204 as deliberate and fails CLOSED (a handler that claims no content while carrying a @ResponseSchema, or without @HttpCode(204), ends up with NO contract rather than a false one), and isVacuousSchema() rejects a root that says nothing -- {}, a bare {type:"object"}, an open additionalProperties record, an array of those, or an allOf/anyOf/oneOf whose every member is vacuous -- so a handler cannot be counted as covered by declaring z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()). Three schemas that had been parked as loose records were written out against their real handler returns in the same change (CRM import preview, leads import batch, org-hierarchy tree). The ceiling is now a hard 100% requirement: any new handler without a response contract reds this gate.

PROVIDER_REACH_MAX_DEPTH.reason: Traversal depth cap for provider reach. Registered PINNED, not as a ratchet or a floor, by v2 ticket 30 on 2026-09-03: ticket 30 does not own this script and did not reason about which direction is safe here, and `pinned` is the honest default -- it asserts no direction and forces whoever changes the constant to re-register it with a direction and a reason. Lowering it shrinks the corpus the gate reaches, which is the vacuity risk; raising it only costs time. Reclassify when the owning ticket lands.

CONDITIONAL_BASELINE.reason: Runtime-selected describes. LOWERED 29 -> 20 on 2026-09-07, and the count itself went 76 -> 20, because the class was RETIRED rather than repriced. The 56 *.db.spec.ts files each opened with `const describeDb = ENABLED && DB_URL ? describe : describe.skip`; that ternary existed only because the default jest run walked those files on machines with no database. They are now selected by suite instead, exactly as *.e2e-spec.ts already was — jest-db.json selects the 56, `pnpm test:db-specs` runs them, and the default jest config ignores \.db\.spec\.ts$ — so the gate became redundant and was deleted. Each spec now THROWS naming the variable it needs when its database is absent, so a missing prerequisite is a red suite and can no longer skip. 19 of the 56 also carried a hermetic half that ran in the default suite; that half was split into a sibling *.spec.ts rather than allowed to fall out of the run silently (16 files, 71 tests, all passing with no database, counted before and after). The 20 survivors are genuinely infrastructure-gated: 9 *.eval.spec.ts needing an AI provider key, 6 src/degradation/** needing a real S3/Ably/read-replica, and the seeded-E2E and perf specs that need specific tenant fixtures to mean anything. This also dissolves the recorded tension with PRD-C018: a new *.db.spec.ts now joins jest-db.json and adds nothing to this class. A ratchet is lowered to the measured value, never raised to fit one.
